title: Prettier and Git
idea: Prettier rewrites code into one agreed style. Git saves the project as commits you can return to, and `.gitignore` keeps secrets and rebuilt files out.
points: Prettier rewrites code into one style, so reviews show logic, not spacing.
`.prettierrc` holds the style rules; `npx prettier . --write` applies them.
A commit saves a snapshot of the files you chose with `git add`.
`.gitignore` lists paths Git skips, such as `node_modules/` and `.env`.

walk.text: Make the project folder and turn it into a repository on `main`.
A stand-in `node_modules`, as `npm install` would create it.
A secret file and a manifest. Git has not seen either yet.
`??` marks untracked files. Without `.gitignore`, `.env` and `node_modules/` are listed.
Create `.gitignore`, one path per line. A trailing slash matches folders only.
`.env` and `node_modules/` are gone from the list.
Stage what is left and commit it. The secret never enters the history.

pitfalls: Pin Prettier with `--save-exact`: different versions can format the same code differently.
Run `git status` before `git add .`; anything not ignored gets staged, secrets included.
Format the whole project once, in its own commit, so feature diffs stay readable.

quiz.q: `.env` was committed earlier. You then ignore it and edit it. What does the last line print?
quiz.why: Ignore rules only cover untracked files. `.env` is already tracked, so Git still reports the edit. Replace any secret that was committed.

takeaway: Format automatically, commit often, and keep secrets out of Git.
